title: Safety audit: update_each groups hashers by comparing their secret keys
body:
Source finding, not a measured attack. `each.rs::hash_held` (next fbfb319f/ddb7199d, and released main 6e0dffd3 line 152) partitions a turn's held hashers with `hashers[i].core.key == key && flags == flags`.

For keyed hashing that compares secret keys:

- `[u32; 8] ==` may stop at the first differing word, so its time can depend on how many leading key words match;
- the result chooses the work: hashers whose keys equal the first held hasher's hash together, the rest in a later pass. Turn time therefore depends on key equality, a larger signal than the comparison itself.

A cursory reader keying one Hasher per tenant or per connection (`Mode::Keyed`) and calling `update_each` sees nothing in the docs about key-dependent timing. #267 states the intended contract: "Control flow and memory access depend on public input shapes, independently of key and message values." Plausible harm: a tenant who controls their own key and can time shared turns obtains an equality oracle against co-resident keys. Prefix leakage through the comparison is smaller and noisier.

I have not measured timing or built an attack; severity rests on the contract. Options, your call: `constant_time_eq` (already a dependency) for the comparison, which removes the prefix signal but keeps the equality-dependent grouping; documenting that `update_each`'s speed reveals whether hashers share a key; or grouping by something public. #281 and #280 are the mixed-key work; I have not changed them.

— Sam Shackleton
